$comment: Authored port of the hand-written registry group ecr-tags (docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md §3.11, G6 wave 3, #1116). The group's only native is the cli suite's (compat/suites/cli/internal/groups/ecr.go); go-sdk, python-sdk, node-js-sdk, java-sdk, dotnet-sdk and rust-sdk never implemented it and carry it as parity debt, which the port closes. It runs as ecr-tags-shadow beside that native until a nightly --compare-shadow agrees; the clauses are what the native asserts — see compat/model/README.md § Authored scenarios.

groups.$comment: Setup creates one repository, as the native's does, and exports its ARN, which every test addresses it by. It is named by $name — {runId}-ecr-tags-shadow-repo — so it is never the native group's (whose namer is ecr-tag) or another ECR group's. Teardown mirrors the native's: both tag keys are removed before the repository, because ECR does not document tags as cascading with it, then the repository is deleted with force. The tag pairs are the native's: env=compat and owner=ecr-tags. No clause is wrapped in `eventually`: the native reads every write back immediately and polls nothing.
groups.name: ecr-tags-shadow

tests.$comment: The native tags env=compat and owner=ecr-tags, then reads the set back and requires both pairs. TagResource returns nothing to check, so both clauses are the read-back.
tests.name: TagResource

tests.$comment: The native requires exactly the two tags TagResource set: a map of two keys, env=compat and owner=ecr-tags. The IR has no length check, so `exactly two` is spelled as a second item present and a third missing, and the two pairs are each required by listContains. Two distinct pairs among exactly two items is the native's map.
tests.name: ListTagsForResource

tests.$comment: The native removes owner, then reads the set back and requires owner gone and env=compat kept. UntagResource returns nothing to check, so both clauses are the read-back.
tests.name: UntagResource
